sampling_model.design: Two independent fixed-size arms sample from \(K\) equal-probability covariate cells. The primary parameter is a pair of deterministic sign arrays in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\). The lower experiment is indexed by \(q\in\mathcal R_K^{\circ}(r)\) and mixes only over the legal shell \(|\rho_K-q|\le s_K\).
sampling_model.units: Within each arm, observations are independent. Conditional on a sampled cell, the outcome is Bernoulli with the cell probability \(p_{dj}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Arm membership is fixed by the two-sample design; treatment and control samples are independent and no unit appears in both arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell has sampling probability \(1/K\) in each arm, while cross-arm overlap is governed by \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The amplitudes \(a\) and \(b\) are known. The sign arrays are unrestricted apart from membership in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\); the procedure estimates their empirical cross-arm correlation only through collision marks. Continuous transfer uses \(U_{di}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and is compared with the discrete design only after the measurable pushforward \(\mathsf Q_K\).

body.tldr: For binary outcomes on a growing uniform covariate partition, the sharp absolute-cost COT lower endpoint is \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\), with \(\rho_K\) the realized correlation of two deterministic sign arrays. When \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\) stays finite and triple collisions vanish, a Poisson number of cross-arm collisions carries the minimax information: parameter-free supported-mixture kernels and a uniform deterministic-array collision approximation yield exact minimax absolute-risk and honest-length transfer, together with shrinking rational interval-action certificates whose tail, off-grid coverage, and rounding errors are explicit. When \(\lambda_K\) diverges sparsely, the unprojected estimator is uniformly studentized Gaussian and the matching deterministic-shell local minimax theorem gives the interior variance frontier. Embedding cell \(j\) as \(j/K\) shows that these finite and local frontiers are converse lower bounds for every anchor-admissible class containing the submodel; this transfer is converse-only. Achievability outside the arrays remains limited to the declared continuous growing-roughness interpolation image, because coarsening can change the endpoint without a separate bias bound.

project_justification.gap: Published COT theory supplies the general sharp conditional-transport endpoint and statistical guarantees under its own regularity regimes, but it does not characterize the marked-Poisson information experiment created by sparse cross-arm replication on a growing partition. Large-alphabet collision theory and confidence-set duality supply ingredients, not the two-arm realized endpoint, certified interval-action enclosure, deterministic-array transfer, or the maximal converse for every anchor class containing that submodel.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a single information frontier indexed by expected cross-arm collisions: exact finite-information decisions when \(\lambda_K\) is bounded, Gaussian local efficiency when it diverges sparsely, and an explicit statement of which conclusions pass from the finite stress test to broader COT classes.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a marked-Poisson reduction with parameter-free forward and reverse randomization under shell-conditioned legal mixtures, derives uniform collision approximation for every deterministic array, certifies finite-information intervals by exact rational lower-dual and upper-primal witnesses with continuum coverage repair, and establishes the ordered LAN-to-deterministic-shell local minimax theorem. The finite arrays embed into the compact-domain Bernoulli-design COT anchor, so subclass monotonicity transfers both finite-intensity frontiers and the local truncated-quadratic variance as converse lower bounds to every containing class. Collision-based upper bounds are not claimed for those broader classes; continuous achievability remains confined to the explicit interpolation image.

body.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS, Theorems 1--6) establish general sharp COT bounds, continuity, and statistical guarantees. Their Theorem~1, under compact covariate and outcome domains and a continuous objective, is the identification anchor: the affine binary endpoint here is a directly proved specialization, and the embedded arrays satisfy that anchor setup. The new anchor-containing-class result transfers collision lower bounds upward only by submodel monotonicity; it does not claim that the collision procedures furnish upper bounds over Lin et al.'s broader class, and alternating embedded signs need not satisfy later uniform smoothness or rate hypotheses. Their smooth-density follow-up (2026) uses Proposition~3.2 for the key estimation bound, Proposition~3.3 for quadratic-objective stability, and Theorem~3.2 for asymptotic normality; atomic binary outcomes and absolute cost require different marked-collision likelihood theory. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.5) provide model-agnostic dual inference and emphasize binning loss, but do not optimize honest expected length or identify the collision frontier. Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) derives sharp OT intervals and root-\(n\) sample-analogue inference in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model, not sparse covariate collisions. Paninski (2008) and Kipnis (2026) show that collisions govern sparse large-alphabet testing; Kipnis's supported-mixture architecture is especially close, but its object is one-sample uniformity testing. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, Theorem~1) supply the dependency-neighborhood Poisson approximation. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem~1 and Corollary~1) supply test inversion and Bayes--minimax duality, while Stoye (2009, Propositions~1--2) diagnoses boundary failures; neither supplies the tail truncation, likelihood modulus, endpoint expansion, full-interval repair, or exact rational verification used here. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem~3) provide a limit-experiment efficiency template; the completed supported-shell argument establishes the ordered deterministic-array local minimax theorem for bounded truncated quadratic losses. Low and Zhou (2007) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2021) motivate the restricted pushforward and bias-aware scope, without supporting an upper claim over a full smoothness ball.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The former two-fixed-array lower witness is invalid because armwise marginal imbalance reveals the endpoint without cross-arm collisions. Every lower bound in this core therefore uses mixtures supported on legal arrays and targets the realized \(L_K\). Floating-point linear-program output may only suggest candidate witnesses: a certificate exists only after every likelihood and tail coefficient is outward-rounded and the resulting rational primal and dual inequalities are verified exactly. Endpoint decisions may be clipped to \(\mathcal D\) without increasing absolute or squared loss, but projection of the statistic \(\widehat L_K\) onto the narrower range \(\mathcal A\) is excluded from the local Gaussian theorem because it changes boundary risk.
body.honest_scope: The proved finite-\(\lambda\) comparison and decision theorems concern the realized endpoint \(L_K\) over the full legal deterministic-array class. The rational interval certificates cover computable \(\lambda\) and require outward-rounded likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual checks; floating-point solver output alone remains outside the claim. The sparse theorem gives unprojected studentized Gaussian inference and the matching ordered deterministic-shell local minimax variance at interior correlations. The embedded finite-array laws meet the compact-domain, continuous-cost COT identification anchor, so their global and local minimax lower bounds transfer to every containing anchor-admissible class; this is a converse-only statement and supplies no collision-based upper bound or equality on a broader class. Continuous achievability transfers only through the declared interpolation-image pushforward. No raw total-variation comparison is made between mutually singular continuous covariates and discrete labels, and no claim is made for unknown amplitudes, nonuniform cell probabilities, nonnegligible triple collisions, dense cellwise estimation, or a full continuous smoothness class. Coarsening changes the estimand unless a separate bias theorem is supplied.
